description:
ObjectStorage.list/3 returns a bare Enumerable.t(), which has no way to say "I failed" - a stream can only yield elements or end. So the S3 backend halted on error (s3.ex) and the local backend skipped directories it could not read, and both were indistinguishable from a prefix that is genuinely empty. Two consumers read that silence as fact, and both lose data.

SHIPPED as PR #202 (stacked on #200).

CHAIN ONE - a RUNNING materializer silently skips committed transactions:
ChunkReader.list_chunks -> empty listing -> Demux.ShardServer.get_from_storage returns {:ok, []} (its rescue only catches failures from READING a chunk, never from failing to LIST them) -> do_pull falls through to the in-memory buffer -> {:ok, []} -> the materializer's pull_once matches its heartbeat clause, fabricates currency at the high-water, and advances next_version past every version it never received. The worker then serves reads as though complete.

CHAIN TWO - a STARTING materializer comes up empty for a populated shard:
Snapshot.read_latest saw [] and returned not_found; Olivine's load_snapshot_from_object_storage read that as "no snapshot exists", logged "starting fresh", and opened an empty database.

WHY THE LISTING IS THE ROOT AND NOT A SYMPTOM: chunks are NEVER deleted (demux/shard_server.ex:324) - there is no retention floor for shard chunks - so {:ok, []} is SUPPOSED to mean "this shard has no data in that range", which is exactly why the heartbeat-and-advance is correct in normal operation. The only thing that makes it wrong is a listing reporting emptiness it never verified.

THE FIX IS THAT THE LISTING STOPS LYING, AND NOTHING ELSE. Backends raise ObjectStorage.ListError; everything downstream was already correct and is untouched: get_from_storage's rescue converts it, do_pull propagates, pull_once takes its existing error branch, fail_over marks the source, and the circuit breaker backs off and retries. Verified end to end against a real ShardServer and the real puller: next_version does NOT advance, and the loop backs off at 1s rather than spinning.

ChunkReader needed no change beyond a comment: it already promises no silent replay gaps (it raises ReadError when a header will not decode, for exactly this reason), and a short listing was that same gap arriving underneath it.

Snapshot DOES translate, because it is the one place emptiness is a legitimate answer: not_found means "no durable baseline, an empty start is correct", and a failed listing must never be able to say that. It surfaces as list_failed so startup fails instead of assuming. Its sibling functions split the same way: latest_version has an error channel and uses it; exists? and count do not, and there is no honest boolean or count for "I could not look", so they raise and say so.

:enoent and :enotdir stay benign in the local backend (absence, and the module already maps :enotdir to not_found); every other errno means we could not see what is there. The walk also stops descending into subtrees that cannot contain a matching key, so one unreadable shard directory no longer aborts a healthy sibling's listing.

RELATED, STILL OPEN: bedrock-q67.21.19 - unparseable object keys are still silently dropped one layer up, the same conflation in a different place.
title: [BUG] S3 list swallows every backend error as an empty listing
